To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the principles and methods of EBM have a great deal to offer the laboratory scientist and that the application of EBM in the laboratory setting can be expected to improve the quality of research, the speed and efficiency of biomarker development and validation, and the clinical utility of biomarkers.

1) the application of the principles of EBM to the laboratory sciences will help to improve the quality of biomarker discovery and development; and 2) the application of EBM to biomarker discovery, development, and application will improve the quality of clinical decision making.

(a) EBM can be successfully applied in the laboratory setting; (b) the application of EBM principles to laboratory science can improve the quality and reproducibility of laboratory science; and (c) this improved quality and reproducibly of laboratory science can lead to better biomarker discovery, validation, and application.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing and applying biomarkers of cardiovascular disease (CVD) in order to better predict and prevent CVD in the population at large.
the development of a novel approach to the design of biomarker studies.
the discovery of new biomarkers for early detection and prognosis of cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the application of EBM in the laboratory sciences is not only possible, but is a necessary component of the development of biomarkers that will be useful in clinical decision making.
the application of EBM principles in basic science research is not only feasible but desirable and will ultimately lead to better science and better clinical practice.
EBM is not just for clinicians, and that many of the principles of EBM are applicable to the discovery and validation of biomarkers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EBM is a powerful tool that should be applied to all aspects of translational research, from the bench to the bedside.
the lessons of EBP are applicable to all aspects of biomarker development and application.
EBM is a useful tool in the development of biomarkers, as long as we remember that biomarkers are not the same as drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the same critical thinking skills that are essential to good clinical practice can also be used to improve the quality of basic science research.
, although EBM was initially developed in the context of clinical medicine, it can and should be used in all areas of biomedical research, from the laboratory to the clinic.
the same principles of critical appraisal and scientific skepticism that are so useful in clinical medicine can be applied to the laboratory sciences.
